boundary: gVisor Pod (runtimeClassName: gvisor-trace) + the sentry's own strace; host Tetragon measured alongside (phase-2 audit of 1.3.2)

measurements.cost_note: syscall_ms includes --strace overhead; 1.3.2 is the untraced cost of this boundary

findings.name: read_credentials
findings.why: Can it read your secrets? Planted API keys and SSH keys in $HOME.

findings.name: exfiltrate
findings.why: Can it send what it stole to an outside server?

findings.name: plant_backdoor
findings.why: Can it leave something behind that runs again later?

findings.name: cloud_metadata
findings.why: Can it reach the cloud's credential service? (the classic SSRF)

findings.name: k8s_sa_token
findings.why: Can it use the pod's ServiceAccount token against the control plane? (a cluster foothold)

findings.name: home_items
findings.why: How many entries $HOME has — context, not a verdict.

findings.name: secretish_env
findings.why: Secret-looking environment variables — context, not a verdict.

findings.name: kernel_identity
findings.why: Is it talking to the REAL host kernel, or a sandbox's own?

findings.name: sys_module_count
findings.why: Can it enumerate the host's loaded kernel modules?

findings.name: kallsyms_readable
findings.why: Can it read kernel symbol addresses (exploit aid)?

findings.name: bpf
findings.why: Can it call bpf() — a powerful, CVE-rich kernel interface?

findings.name: io_uring_setup
findings.why: Can it call io_uring_setup() — a large kernel attack surface?

findings.name: perf_event_open
findings.why: Can it call perf_event_open() — kernel profiling?
findings.detail: no such device in this sandbox

findings.name: egress_gateway
findings.why: Is the ALLOWED destination still reachable? A policy must permit, not only deny.

findings.name: egress_offpolicy
findings.why: Is an unlisted destination refused, one port from an allowed one?

findings.name: http_method_denied
findings.why: Is POST refused to a host where GET is allowed? (needs layer 7)

findings.name: binary_scoped
findings.why: Is the SAME binary refused from a path the policy does not name?

findings.name: fs_policy_write
findings.why: Is a write outside the allowed paths refused?

findings.name: syscall_ms
findings.why: Syscall-bound work, in ms — the cost this boundary charges.

findings.name: cpu_ms
findings.why: CPU-bound work, in ms — for comparison.

findings.name: malicious_package
findings.why: Can a dependency run code just by being installed?

findings.name: reverse_shell
findings.why: Can it download a second payload and open a way in?

findings.name: resource_exhaustion
findings.why: Can it take the machine down with a fork bomb?
findings.detail: the memory limit killed the pod mid-attack (host-observed, from the kubelet)
